open_obligations: Check Proposition 7's proof in Appendix C.1 (p22 L42 onward) against the exact hypotheses of Anil et al.'s verifier-leading theorem
Confirm that Anil et al.'s theorem assumes a deterministic single-message prover and a verifier strategy set of convex combinations of deterministic functions, as the authors state

Note the setting difference: Proposition 7 is stated for a probabilistic decision problem (X, S, P) and an adp game in which some valid interactive proof protocol with ϵc = 0 exists, while Theorem 2 concerns desirable (complete and sound) protocols in verifier-leading sequential formulations where the problem instance is revealed after the verifier picks its strategy; the limit applies to Theorem 2 only if Proposition 7's game meets that hypothesis
out.other_title: PVG: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff complete and sound protocol
out.rationale: The authors do not dispute Anil et al.'s theorem under its stated assumptions but prove that the correspondence fails when those assumptions are relaxed, and say these restrictions (a prover that deterministically sends a single message and a verifier strategy set of convex combinations of deterministic functions) limit the power of the protocol. This shows a limit of the cited result rather than arguing that it is flawed, so CHALLENGES.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: Whether equilibria of a one-message prover-verifier game correspond to valid interactive proofs; the authors say the limit applies when the restrictions to a deterministic prover and a verifier mixing deterministic functions are relaxed, though Proposition 7 keeps a deterministic prover strategy δp

text: The authors note that Anil et al. show a correspondence between equilibria of their single-message 'Abstract Decision Problem' (adp) game and valid proof systems when the prover is deterministic and the verifier mixes deterministic functions. They argue these restrictions limit the protocol's power and give Proposition 7, an adp game in which being a verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium is neither necessary nor sufficient for validity once the assumptions are relaxed.
title: Hammond et al. argue Anil et al.'s adp equilibrium-proof correspondence holds only narrowly
